If accuracy improves with more distinct paths even when total tokens are held constant, the hypothesis is supported; if token budget alone explains gains, it is refuted.

[PATH:theoretical] Theoretical analysis of the probability of hitting a correct solution path as a function of sampling diversity in tree-structured reasoning spaces, using concepts from Monte Carlo estimation and coverage probability. — Provides a formal framework to predict when path diversity (vs. token length) dominates performance, especially under backtracking requirements. This can derive testable bounds and conditions that confirm or refute the empirical pattern.
